lessons.title: What is AI? ChatGPT and Gemini

steps.title: What is artificial intelligence (AI)?
steps.body: AI (artificial intelligence) refers to computer programs that have learned to understand language and generate text, answers, or images themselves. Well-known examples are ChatGPT (by OpenAI) and Gemini (by Google).

steps.title: Chatting with an AI
steps.body: You type a question or instruction (a 'prompt') into a text box, for example 'Explain what inflation is in simple terms'. Within seconds you get a reply. You can then ask follow-up questions, just like in a conversation.

steps.title: What AI is — and isn't — good at
steps.body:
AI is good at: summarizing text, explaining things, brainstorming ideas, writing a first draft.

AI is not always reliable: it can 'make up' things that sound correct but aren't true (this is called a hallucination). Always double-check important facts yourself.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Open Gemini below and ask a simple question, for example 'What can I cook today with potatoes and chicken?'

steps.title: What is a 'prompt'?
steps.body: A prompt is the question or instruction you give to an AI. The clearer your prompt, the better the answer.

steps.title: Tips for a good prompt
steps.body:
• Be specific: instead of 'write a letter', try 'write a short, friendly letter to my neighbor about a leaking gutter'
  • Give context: mention who the answer is for, and why
  • Ask for a specific format: 'in at most 5 sentences', 'as a step-by-step list'
  • Not happy with the result? Just ask it to try again differently or shorter

steps.title: Examples of good prompts
steps.body:
• 'Explain in simple terms what 2FA is, as if I've never heard of internet security.'
  • 'Write a birthday message for my 10-year-old grandson who loves football.'
  • 'Make a shopping list for a lasagna for 4 people.'
  • 'Summarize this email in 3 sentences: [paste the text here]'

steps.title: What happens to what you type?
steps.body: What you type into an AI chat is sent to and processed by the company behind that AI (for example Google or OpenAI). That's not the same as a private conversation.

steps.title: What you should never share with an AI chatbot
steps.body:
• Passwords or login codes
  • Your DigiD details or national ID number
  • Bank details or PIN codes
  • Medical records containing other people's names
  • Sensitive information about other people

steps.title: Checking answers
steps.body: An AI often sounds confident, even when the answer is wrong. Always check important information (medical, financial, legal) with an official source or expert before acting on it.

steps.title: AI is not a doctor, lawyer, or bank
steps.body: Don't use AI as a substitute for professional advice. For medical concerns, go to your doctor (or a trusted medical source), for legal questions go to a lawyer, and for money matters go to your bank or an advisor.

steps.title: Important or official decisions
steps.body: Never base an official decision solely on an AI answer, such as a tax return, a medical treatment, or a major purchase. Always verify this with a person or an official body.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body: Think of AI as a tool — handy for getting ideas, checking text, or having something explained — but not as an infallible truth. When in doubt: ask a person.
